title: finding(app-shell/plugin-grid): the target-required degrade set `{lookup, master_detail}` is stated once per package, with nothing tying the two
body:
Measured while implementing #5654 (which converged the app-shell side). **Out of that card's fence** — its surface is `paramToField.ts` + `ActionParamDialog.tsx` + their tests — so this is filed rather than fixed in passing.

## What is there

The **target-required** rule ("this picker widget cannot query without a DECLARED target, so degrade it to a plain text input") is a different rule from the reference-bearing family in #5874 / #5875: it is a smaller set over the same types, and #5312 kept the two deliberately separate because `user` is reference-bearing but must never degrade.

After #5654 that rule has exactly one statement per package, and there are two packages:

| file | the statement | keyed on |
|---|---|---|
| `packages/app-shell/src/utils/paramToField.ts:54` | `LOOKUP_WIDGET_TYPES = new Set(['lookup', 'master_detail'])`, read by the exported `paramDegradesWithoutTarget(param)` | `ActionParamDef.referenceTo` |
| `packages/plugin-grid/src/components/bulkParamToField.ts:40` | `LOOKUP_WIDGET_TYPES = new Set(['lookup', 'master_detail'])`, read inline in `bulkParamToField` | `BulkActionParam.object` |

Members are identical today, so **there is no measured divergence** — this is the latent kind, not a live defect.

## Why it is worth a card anyway

The two are documented as twins ("mirrors app-shell's `paramToField`", "same last-resort fallback as app-shell's `paramToField`"), and nothing mechanical holds them together: no shared object, no pin, no gate that could report a split. That is exactly the state #5312 measured and falsified for the *sibling* rule in the same two files — the comment there claimed the two faces "move in lockstep" while they had already drifted by a member and shared nothing.

Cost if it drifts: a third picker widget that needs a declared target gets added to one set. The bulk dialog then silently stops degrading it — a picker that cannot query, rendered as a picker.

## Not obviously mergeable — that is the decision to make

The predicates read different fields on different types (`ActionParamDef.referenceTo` vs `BulkActionParam.object`), so this is not a lift-and-share the way `EXPANDABLE_FIELD_TYPES` was. Options, unranked:

- share the **member set** only (a small exported constant, each surface keeping its own "has a target?" half);
- pin the two sets equal in a test that names the other package;
- rule the duplication acceptable and say so in both files, so the next reader stops re-deciding.

## References

- #5654 (this rule's app-shell convergence), #5312 (the sibling rule; kept them separate on purpose)
- #5874 / #5875 (the *reference-bearing* family — related lineage, different rule)
